pr.title: The UI's first version, implemented: transport and lanes over the files, with mute and solo
pr.head: eb413a8918ec100dee7372d777d4bad528d056d7

summary: Field is a Git-native music production tool: a song is a directory of YAML files, a build graph renders them into stems, and a native daemon, field-audiod, plays the result. Until this pull request, you worked with a song through CLI commands and hand edits. It adds field ui <song>, a desktop window onto a playing song.

The files stay the only store. field ui runs a local HTTP and WebSocket server inside field's own Node process, and a React client talks to it from an Electron window or a browser tab. Every gesture that changes the song ends as a YAML edit written through the same comment-preserving Document machinery the CLI's editors use. The existing watch loop then carries the file change into the playing session, exactly as it does for a hand edit. Each edit carries the sha256 of the file bytes it was derived from, and the server refuses a stale one and refreshes the view instead of writing through.

• Mute. A new mute: field on a placement, beside gain_db and pan. The build graph leaves muted placements out of the plan.
  • Solo. A session-only alternate feed: the server compiles a filtered copy of the song and swaps it into the daemon, and nothing is written.
  • Timeline. One row per placement, nested rows for placed tracks, waveforms, and clip move, split, and front and end trim.
  • Insert panel. Add, edit, and remove built-in effects on a track, with an EQ curve drawn by a TypeScript port of the native biquad arithmetic.
  • Plans. The UI plan flips to in-progress with a new §6, two other plans gain amendments, and a draft daw-features catalogue arrives.

The Projector review at eb413a8 requests changes with 21 open finding threads: one P1, where editing one insert knob resets the insert's other authored parameters, and twenty P2s. They are flagged under the lines they concern below. The head is untrusted, because its author has no write access to the repository, so the review read the code and ran none of it.

cards.title: Terms used on this page
cards.html:
• Placement or entry: one item in a track file's inputs: list, such as - track: drums or - audio: riff, with its position, length, level, and fades.
  • Lane or row: the timeline's drawing of one placement. Its entry is the placement's index in inputs:.
  • Send, receive, cable: a track's sends: feed a labelled cable, and a - receive: label entry in another track hears it, for example a shared reverb.
  • Stem: a track's rendered audio file. A frozen track is served to the daemon as its cached stem instead of being evaluated live.
  • Swap and ramp: the two ways the watch loop updates a playing session. A swap replaces the session, and a ramp moves one gain in place.
  • Carrier: under solo, a track the soloed track is heard through on its way to main.
  • Stale-hash guard: the check that an edit's sha256 still matches the file on disk.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• The author's own reviews. eve-nyx-13 reviewed each push of this branch, from August 18 to August 22. Five of those threads are still open and are the author's to resolve. At eb413a8, the receive-index and duration-spelling ones are fixed, and the fades one is fixed for trims.
  • Review on 04a0857. A Projector review requested changes with two findings. The duplicate UI plan is fixed, because the plan now lives once, at docs/projects/ui/readme.md. The ui/dist prefix finding was withdrawn as unreachable, and 4b500ad hardened it anyway.
  • Review on eb413a8. Requested changes with 21 threads. It started on 612f0c1 and followed two pushes: cdd4388 fixed the Linux build (a missing <cmath>), and eb413a8 fixed four earlier findings and merged the base.

cards.title: What each socket operation writes
cards.html:
OperationWritesInto
editgain_db, pan, or muteThe placement's owner file
moveat, in the author's spellingThe placement's owner file
splitTwo entries cloned from one, with duration, at, and source_offsetThe placement's owner file
stretchEnd: duration. Start: at, duration, and source_offsetThe placement's owner file
insert-add, insert-edit, insert-removeThe track's inserts: chainThe track's own file
soloNothing: the server swaps a filtered sessionNone
play, pause, stop, locate, deviceNothing: daemon transport commandsNone

groups.title: Mute and solo in the engine
groups.kicker: A placement field the build graph drops, and a filtered copy of the song for solo
intro: Mute is a boolean on a placement, stored in the file like gain_db. It is a field rather than a gain gesture because a gesture would overwrite the authored level, and remembering the old level anywhere but the file would be a second store. planFor in graph.ts filters muted placements out before anything else reads the track, so the stem's spec, its cache key, and the live session all leave them out.

Solo is a listening gesture, so it lives in the running session and is never written. soloView in solo.ts walks the song and keeps three groups: the soloed track's own subtree, its carriers with only the inputs that lead to it, and the receivers of its sends. compileSession applies that filter to the loaded song before it builds the graph.
The build.ts changes are separate: they let a rebuild replace a stem that a Windows daemon holds open, and stop leaking temporary copies when it cannot.

checks.text: Cable arrivals are computed in src/model/cables.ts, which this pull request does not change and which does not read mute. Read the graph.ts filter with that in mind.

files.note: Adds mute: z.boolean().default(false) to a placement, and puts mute after pan in the canonical key order.

checks.text: P2 review finding: The root docs do not describe mute: or field ui Fix: Add mute to docs/tracks.md and docs/build-graph.md, and describe field ui and its solo in docs/architecture.md.

files.note: The one-line filter in planFor that drops muted placements before the track is planned.

checks.text: P2 review finding: A muted placement keeps playing through its sends, in playback and in exports Fix: Skip muted edges when cables.ts collects sender placements for arrivals, treat a cable whose sender placements are all muted as silent rather than unjoined, and cover it with a test.

files.note: The solo walk: the soloed subtree, carriers, and send receivers, then applySolo filters each track's inputs and the cable list in place.
compileSession takes solo and applies it to the loaded song before building the graph.

checks.text: P2 review finding: A held solo can play the un-soloed mix of a track whose soloed shape was built before Fix: Under a solo, serve each frozen track from its own explanation's cached output instead of buildLabels, or never freeze a track whose inputs or cables applySolo changed.

files.note: renameOverwrite retries a rename that Windows refuses while the daemon holds the stem open, and materialize skips the copy when the output already has the same bytes. The head's merge keeps this beside main's fetchAction.

groups.title: The wire protocol
groups.kicker: The messages between the server and the client, as TypeScript types
intro: ui-protocol.ts defines what the server sends down: a snapshot of the song, transport, devices, and timeline, daemon events such as position, and errors. The client imports the types, so a change to one side that the other cannot read fails the typecheck. The messages the client sends up are zod schemas in ui.ts, because the server must validate them.

files.note: The snapshot, event, and timeline-lane types. A lane's entry is the placement's index in its file's inputs:.

groups.title: Arithmetic the client shares with the engine
groups.kicker: Tempo and meter conversions and the EQ response, importable by the browser
intro: The client runs its own playhead between the daemon's 250 ms position events, so it needs the tempo and meter maps. It imports src/time/tempo.ts directly rather than porting it, so the two cannot drift. MeterMap gains position and span, the inverses of positionTicks and spanTicks, which the edits use to keep the author's bar-and-beat spelling.

The EQ editor redraws its curve during a drag, so eq-response.ts ports the native biquad design, magnitude, and auto-gain to TypeScript. The render still runs only in the daemon. A test holds the port equal to the C++ through a new eq-response mode in field-dsp-check.

files.note: Adds MeterMap.position, which turns ticks into [bar, beat, tick], and MeterMap.span, which turns ticks into a span from an anchor.
A line-for-line port of design, magnitudeDb, and autoGainDb from biquad.cpp, for drawing only.
An eq-response mode that prints the native curve and auto-gain for given bands, so a test can compare the port against it. cdd4388 added the <cmath> include that Linux needed.

groups.title: The field ui server
groups.kicker: One process that owns the session, the socket, and every write
intro: runUi compiles the session, connects to the daemon, and starts the watch loop. It then serves the built client and accepts WebSockets only on /ws, with a matching Origin and the per-launch token. Each message is validated with zod and dispatched: transport commands go to the daemon, solo recompiles and swaps the session, and file edits resolve the owner file, check the hash, call a pure function in ui-edits.ts, and write the result. Snapshots go out through one promise chain and only when they differ, which stopped the flicker earlier commits fought.
At the end it opens the Electron shell, or a browser tab with --browser, and waits for Ctrl-C or for the shell to exit.

checks.text: Writes happen in the handlers here, while the text they write comes from ui-edits.ts. Several findings are about what a handler checks before it writes, so read the two side by side.

files.note: The server: upgrade guards, message schemas, the snapshot chain, the watch-loop hooks, the edit handlers, static files, the shell launch, and teardown.

checks.text: P2 review finding: Moves and splits can write a file the next load refuses, turning the song red Fix: Validate the edited text with the loader's diagnostics before each writeFileSync, and refuse the gesture with the first new diagnostic instead of writing it.

P2 review finding: Every recompile that changes nothing reloads the whole daemon session Fix: When edit.kind === 'same', call only pushSnapshot(), which still carries a comment-only edit's new hash to the view.

P2 review finding: Two edits read from one socket chunk both pass the stale-hash check, and the second overwrites the first Fix: Run every file-writing message through one promise chain, so that each operation's read, check, and write finish before the next one reads.

P2 review finding: When the Electron shell fails to start, field ui exits instead of opening a browser Fix: Treat a shell that exits non-zero before any WebSocket connects as a failed start that reports itself, calls openInBrowser(), and keeps the session running, and correct the §5 amendment's post-install wording.

P2 review finding: Closing the UI leaves the song playing, and a connected tab keeps the process alive after Ctrl-C Fix: Before closing the server and the client, stop the transport with await client.stop().catch(() => {}) and call terminate() on every socket in sockets.

P2 review finding: After pause or stop the playhead shows a stale position, and a split cuts there Fix: Handle pause and stop like locate: clear lastSent and push a snapshot, which carries status.sample.

P2 review finding: The cross-rate refusal misses ledger rows without sample_rate, so a split writes the wrong source_offset Fix: Resolve the source's rate the way graph.ts does, with sample_rate ?? headerRate(...), and use sharedAssetName from labels.ts in place of the regular expression.

P2 review finding: Several comments misstate the code or narrate an earlier draft Fix: Correct each misstated comment to match the code (for line 459, hash owner.raw instead of re-reading), and delete the CI variable and the two narrating comments.

files.note: Registers field ui <song> with --port, --no-open, and --browser. The head's merge keeps it beside main's field record.

groups.title: Edits and the timeline projection
groups.kicker: Pure text-to-text YAML edits, and the lanes the view draws
intro: ui-edits.ts holds every file edit as a pure function from document text to document text, so a test can write, read back, and compare bytes. Each one keeps the author's spelling: a musical at: [5] stays an array, defaults stay implicit, and comments survive. Split clones the entry node so both halves keep every field and comment.

ui-timeline.ts turns the loaded song into lanes: one per placement, children for placed tracks, each with its window in session samples, the hash of the file it came from, and a waveform envelope read from the built stem.

files.note: Edit, move, split, stretch, and the three insert operations, each returning the new text or a refusal.

checks.text: P1 review finding: Changing one insert knob resets every other authored parameter on that insert Fix: Iterate the keys of set and take each validated value from parsed.data, and add a test that edits one parameter on an insert whose other parameters are authored.

P2 review finding: A musical split moves the window by whole ticks but the read by raw samples, so the halves stop meeting Fix: For a musical entry, advance source_offset by tempo.ticksToSamples(parsed.at + cut) - w.start, in both the split and the front trim.

files.note: Builds the timeline lanes and their waveform envelopes. 07447dd keeps each lane's index in the unfiltered inputs:, so a receive no longer shifts it.

checks.text: The receive-index fix holds at eb413a8: placements() pairs each non-receive entry with its index in inputs: before filtering, at both the top level and the child rows. Checked by reading 07447dd and its new test.

P2 review finding: Child rows ignore the parent's slip and source offset, so they are drawn and cut at the wrong time Fix: Pass startSample − (source_offset − slip), scaled to the session rate, as the children's origin, and clip child rows to the parent's window.

P2 review finding: A clip without duration is drawn to the song's end, with its waveform stretched to fit Fix: Size an open window from the rendered stem's length minus the placement's read offset, and bucket the envelope over the slice the placement reads.

groups.title: The client and its shell
groups.kicker: A React app in an Electron window, with local state only inside a gesture
intro: App.tsx opens the WebSocket, keeps the latest snapshot, and runs a frame loop that advances the playhead from the last position event. Timeline.tsx draws the ruler, rows, clips, waveforms, and drag handles, and follows the playhead during playback. Inserts.tsx shows the selected track's chain, with knobs for each effect and an EQ curve with draggable bands.
shell.cjs is the Electron main process: one window on the server's URL, with the renderer's console mirrored to the terminal, which is how a blank window was diagnosed.

files.note: The socket, the playhead loop, the transport bar, the lane controls, and the keyboard shortcuts.

checks.text: P2 review finding: Keyboard changes to a fader are never written, and the leftover value lands on the next fader you click Fix: Commit on the input's native change event as well as on pointer-up, and key drag by the lane's tree path instead of entry.

P2 review finding: The playhead loop runs at frame rate while paused, though its comment says it stops Fix: Schedule the next frame only while state === 'playing', and run tick once whenever a snapshot or a locate moves the anchor while paused.

P2 review finding: A song without time: shows a frozen readout and playhead during playback Fix: Without a clock, advance playSample from the anchor at the timeline's rate, and show each position event's musical string as the readout.

files.note: The timeline: rows, clip drags, trims, selection, and the follow-the-playhead scroll.
The insert panel: add and remove effects, knobs, and the EQ editor.

checks.text: P2 review finding: Dragging the EQ width slider writes on every step and keeps an intermediate value Fix: Hold the width in draft during the gesture and commit once on pointerup or keyup, the way the handle drag does.

files.note: The Electron main process: profile directory, window, console mirroring, and the window-open handler.
Hand-rolled styles, including the sticky header column and the clip grips.

checks.text: P2 review finding: Clip edge grips sit above the sticky lane controls, so a fader press can trim a clip Fix: Give .tl-lane its own stacking context, for example with isolation: isolate, so nothing inside a lane can rise above the header column.

files.note: Mounts the app and turns a render crash into a visible message.
The page, with a content security policy limited to the local server.

groups.title: Workspace, dependencies, and CI
groups.kicker: A second pnpm workspace member for the client, and CI that builds it
intro: The client is its own pnpm workspace member, ui/, so its DOM and JSX toolchain stays out of the CLI's strict Node-only config. The root package gains ws for the server. React, Vite, and Electron live only in ui/. CI typechecks and builds the client on Linux.

files.note: Adds ws and @types/ws, and a build:ui script.
The client's dependencies: React 18, Vite 6, and Electron 43.
Declares the two workspace members, . and ui.
Builds ui/ on Linux and sets ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD on both jobs.
The Vite config, with only the React plugin.
The client's own TypeScript config, with DOM types and JSX.

groups.title: Plans
groups.kicker: The UI plan flips to in-progress, two plans record amendments, and a catalogue arrives
intro: The UI plan, docs/projects/ui/readme.md, moves from draft to in-progress at priority: now and gains §6, the record of what the first implementation settled. Every question in §5 is answered or settled, so the flip owes no open question. project-core §5 records the new stack pieces, the ui/ workspace member, ws, React, Vite, and Electron, against its single-package decision. render-pipeline decision 4 records the TypeScript EQ arithmetic as a bounded reversal.
daw-features is a draft catalogue of what users of other DAWs praise and wish for, with what each would mean for Field. It claims no readiness.

files.note: Frontmatter flip, §5's shell question settled, and the new §6.

checks.text: P2 review finding: §6 says everything shipped as §3 wrote it, but the timeline, clip edits, and insert editor are §3 non-goals Fix: Record the timeline, nested rows, clip edits, and insert editor in §6 or in a ui-timeline plan that §6 links, each with why it beat the non-goal, and correct the "shipped as written" and "lanes are flat" statements.

files.note: Two dated amendments to §5's stack record: the workspace member with ws, React, and Vite, and then Electron.
An amendment to decision 4: response arithmetic, never sample processing, exists in TypeScript again, held equal to the C++ by a test.
A draft research catalogue, at priority: later.
